Greenwood County by the numbers

Where is Greenwood County and what towns are in it?

Greenwood County is in the western Piedmont of South Carolina and covers 463.81 square miles, with 455.60 of that land. Greenwood is the county seat and the largest community.

Four other incorporated places sit in the county: Hodges, Ninety Six, Troy and Ware Shoals, and Ware Shoals reaches into Abbeville and Laurens counties. Unincorporated communities include Callison, Epworth, Kirksey, Phoenix, Pittsburg, Shoals Junction and Verdery.

Neighboring countySide
LaurensNorth
NewberryNortheast
Edgefield and SaludaSoutheast
McCormickSouthwest
AbbevilleWest

A house in a small town such as Troy or Hodges sells in a very different pool of buyers than a house in the city of Greenwood, though all of them are taxed through the same courthouse.

How did Greenwood County begin?

Greenwood County was formed in 1897 from parts of Abbeville and Edgefield counties, both once part of the Ninety-Six District. It was named for its seat, and the town took its name around 1824 from a cotton plantation owned by John McGehee.

The 2020 Census counted 69,351 residents, close to the 69,661 counted in 2010. The 2025 estimate is 70,379, so the county is large enough to keep a real market but has not seen the surge some of its neighbors have.

Slow, steady population means many homes here are owned for a long time and pass through families. When an heir ends up with a house in the county that they do not plan to keep, selling for cash can be simpler than a listing.

What is Lake Greenwood and why does it matter to homeowners?

Lake Greenwood was created by the Buzzard's Roost Dam on the Saluda River, which the county page describes as the largest New Deal project in the area. The county later sold the hydroelectric plant to Duke Power Company.

The lake offers recreation for residents and visitors, and many owners near it hold second homes rather than primary residences.

The Auditor says the school-tax credit does not apply to second homes, so a lake house that is not your legal residence is billed differently from a primary home. Ask the Assessor how your parcel is classified.

What industries and employers support Greenwood County?

Health care and social assistance made up 22.1 percent of employment in the third quarter of 2023, manufacturing 19.8 percent and retail trade 12.8 percent.

  • Healthcare and education: Self Regional Healthcare, the Greenwood County school districts, Lander University and Piedmont Technical College.
  • Manufacturing: Eaton Corporation, FujiFilm, Capsugel, Ascend Performance Materials and VELUX.
  • Distribution and health products: Cardinal Health is also on the major employer list.

With a few large employers carrying much of the job base, sellers who need to relocate on a deadline often want a closing date they control.

What highways cross Greenwood County?

US 25 and US 178 are the principal federal routes, with business routes in the city of Greenwood, and US 221 also crosses the county. State routes include SC 10, 34, 72, 246, 248, 252 and 702.

Business routes run through both Greenwood and Ware Shoals, so those towns have main streets that carry through traffic. Distance from a main route is something buyers weigh, and a cash buyer prices it in without asking you to wait for the right match.

Which Greenwood County offices handle property tax?

Three offices at the Greenwood County Courthouse, 528 Monument Street, handle most of the work. Hours at each are 7:45 to 5:30, Monday through Thursday, and they are closed Friday.

OfficeRoomPhoneHandles
Assessor109(864) 942-8537Valuation and appeals
AuditorSuite 107(864) 942-8543Homestead and legal residence credit
Tax Collector101(864) 942-3142Payments, redemptions

The Assessor's staff has five licensed appraisers and four support staff. The office notes that a complaint about the amount of a tax bill cannot be an assessment appeal, since an appeal has to challenge value, use classification or ratio.

How and when do you pay Greenwood County property tax?

Advance installments on real estate are due in February, April, June, August and October, and the final payment is due on or before January 15 of the following year. The county posted this year's bills online on November 4, 2026.

  • You can pay in person, by mail, in the lobby drop box or online through the county's payment vendor.
  • Accepted forms include cash, certified checks, money orders and major credit cards, and a convenience fee may apply to cards.
  • Out-of-state checks are not accepted for delinquent real estate taxes.

The Tax Collector page does not list late penalties. The state schedule in S.C. Code 12-45-180 applies: 3 percent after January 15, a further 7 percent on February 2 and a further 5 percent on March 17. Ask the office to confirm the amount for your bill.

Who qualifies for the homestead exemption and the school-tax credit?

An owner who is 65 or older, totally and permanently disabled, or legally blind can apply for the homestead exemption, provided they hold fee simple title or a life estate in the primary residence. They must have been a South Carolina resident for a calendar year as of December 31 of the preceding tax year.

The Auditor says qualifying legal residents get a 4 percent homeowners credit on school operating taxes and pay only school bond taxes. That credit does not reach second homes, land or business property.

Anyone who sells or rents the home, or changes the owners on the deed, must tell the Auditor. A sale therefore ends the exemption for the seller, and the buyer must apply for their own.

What should you know about appeals and rollback taxes in Greenwood County?

If your notice raised value by $1,000 or more, you have 90 days from mailing to object in writing under S.C. Code 12-60-2510. Send the objection to the Assessor at Room 109.

Agricultural-use land needs at least 5 acres in timber or 10 acres in crops, including pasture. If the use changes, up to five years of taxes can become due, which is a real concern for a seller who is subdividing a family tract.

Builders can seek the exemption for newly built single-family homes, and subdivision lots may qualify for a multiple lot discount. Both are handled through the Assessor.

How does a deed get recorded and what if the tax goes unpaid?

The Register of Deeds is in Room 114 of the courthouse, open 8:30 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. Monday through Friday, at (864) 942-8612. Documents brought in are recorded the same day, though anything after 4 p.m. waits until the next day, and originals are mailed back 3 to 5 business days later.

The recording tax is $1.85 per $500 under Title 12, Chapter 24. State tax liens are no longer filed with county offices and appear on the Department of Revenue's registry.

Tax sale redemptions are handled in Room 101 and accepted only as cash, certified check or money order, never by card. Selling before a sale avoids that route.

More questions about Greenwood County, SC Property Tax Guide

When is the final Greenwood County property tax payment due?

The final payment is due on or before January 15 of the year after the tax year. The county also offers advance installments in February, April, June, August and October.

Can I pay Greenwood County taxes online?

Yes, current and delinquent real, personal and mobile home taxes can be paid online through the county's vendor, as well as in person, by mail or in the lobby drop box. A card fee may apply.

Does Greenwood County offer a homestead exemption?

Yes, for owners 65 or older, totally and permanently disabled, or legally blind who meet ownership and residency rules. Apply in person with the Auditor, and notify the office if you sell or rent.

How long do I have to object to a Greenwood County assessment?

You have 90 days from the mailing of a notice that raised value by $1,000 or more. The objection goes in writing to the Assessor.

What are the office hours for Greenwood County tax offices?

The Assessor, Auditor and Tax Collector keep 7:45 to 5:30 Monday through Thursday and close Friday. The Register of Deeds is open 8:30 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. Monday through Friday.
